'''David A. Evans''' (January 11, 1941 – April 29, 2022)<ref>[https://chemistry.harvard.edu/news/david-evans-1941-2022 David A. Evans (1941-2022)]</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lautens |first=Mark |date=2022-06-23 |title=David A. Evans (1941–2022) |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=606 |issue=7916 |pages=859 |doi=10.1038/d41586-022-01737-5|pmid=35739264 |s2cid=249989990 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2022Natur.606..859L }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=HALFORD |first=BETHANY |date=May 5, 2022 |title=Organic chemist David A. Evans dies at 81 |url=https://cen.acs.org/people/obituaries/Organic-chemist-David-A-Evans-dies-81/100/i16 |journal=Chemical & Engineering News |volume=100 |issue=16}}</ref> was an American chemist who was the Abbott and James Lawrence professor of chemistry at [[Harvard University]].<ref name=cv>{{Cite web|url=http://evans.rc.fas.harvard.edu/cgi-bin/evans.cgi|title=David A. Evans - Curriculum Vitae|last=|first=|date=|website=Harvard University|access-date=March 14, 2017|archive-date=March 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330130930/http://evans.rc.fas.harvard.edu/cgi-bin/evans.cgi|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=facpage>{{Cite web|url=http://chemistry.harvard.edu/people/david-evans|title=David Evans|last=|first=|date=|website=Harvard University|access-date=March 14, 2017}}</ref>  He was a prominent figure in the field of [[organic chemistry]] and his research focused on [[synthetic chemistry]] and [[total synthesis]], particularly of large biologically active molecules.  Among his best-known works is the development of [[aldol reaction]] methodology (for example, [[Aldol reaction#Evans.27 oxazolidinone chemistry|Evans' acyl oxazolidinone method]]).<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Organic Syntheses|date=1990|volume=68|pages=83|doi=10.15227/orgsyn.068.0083|doi-access=free|title=Diastereoselective Aldol Condensation Using a Chiral Oxazolidinone Auxiliary: (2S,3S)-3-Hydroxy-3-Phenyl-2-Methylpropanoic Acid}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Evans was born on January 11, 1941, in [[Washington, D.C.]] He received his [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] from [[Oberlin College]] in 1963, where he worked with Norman Craig.<ref name=evanstet>{{Cite journal|last=Evans|first=David A.|title=A view from the far side. Memorable characters and interesting places|journal=Tetrahedron|language=en|volume=55|issue=29|pages=8589–8608|doi=10.1016/s0040-4020(99)00436-6|year=1999}}</ref> He began his graduate work at the [[University of Michigan]] with [[Robert E. Ireland]], but moved with the Ireland group to the [[California Institute of Technology]] and received his Ph.D. from Caltech in 1967.<ref name=cv /><ref name=facpage /><ref name=evanstet />

==Academic career==
Evans began his independent research career at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], where he joined the faculty in 1967 and became a [[full professor]] in 1973. He then moved to the [[California Institute of Technology]] and remained there until 1983, when he moved again to [[Harvard University]].<ref name=evanstet /> He was appointed the Abbott and James Lawrence Professor of Chemistry in 1990, served as chair of the Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology from 1995 to 1998, and retired from the faculty, assuming [[professor emeritus]] status, in 2008.<ref name=cv /><ref name=facpage />

==Research==
Evans made many scholarly contributions to the field of organic chemistry.<ref name=evanstet /> Although he is best known for his work on the aldol reaction, he also developed methodology for [[anionic]] [[Cope rearrangement|oxy-Cope rearrangement]]s, metal catalyzed [[Hydroboration-oxidation reaction|hydroboration]]s, and [[catalytic]], [[enantioselective]] reactions based on [[bisoxazoline ligand|bis-oxazoline]] (box) [[ligand]]s. The [[Evans–Saksena reduction]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Saksena|first1= Anil|last2= Mangiaracina|first2= Pietro|year= 1983|title= Recent studies on veratrum alkaloids: a new reaction of sodium triacetoxyborohydride [NaBH(OAc)3]|journal= [[Tetrahedron Letters]]|volume=24 |issue= 3|pages= 273–276|doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(00)81383-0 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Evans |first1=David |last2=Chapman |first2= K.|last3=Carreira|first3=E.|year= 1988|title= Directed reduction of β-hydroxy ketones employing tetramethylammonium triacetoxyborohydride|journal= [[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]|volume= 110|issue= 11|pages= 3560–3578|doi= 10.1021/ja00219a035|bibcode=1988JAChS.110.3560E }}</ref> and [[Evans–Tishchenko reaction]] take their names from him.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Evans|first1=David|last2=Hoveyda|first2=Amir|title=Samarium-catalyzed intramolecular Tishchenko reduction of β-hydroxy ketones. A stereoselective approach to the synthesis of differentiated anti 1,3-diol monoesters|journal=[[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]]|year=1990|volume=112|issue=17|pages=6447–6449|doi=10.1021/ja00173a071|bibcode=1990JAChS.112.6447E }}</ref>  He is also well known for preparing a set of unpublished though widely disseminated lecture notes for Chemistry 206, a graduate-level organic chemistry course at Harvard.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Evans|first=David A.|date=2006|title=Harvard's Advanced Organic Chemistry|url=https://archive.org/details/evans-d.-a.-myers-a.-g.-advanced-organic-chemistry-lecture-notes-problem-sets-an|access-date=October 11, 2020|website=Internet Archive}}</ref>
[[File:Оксазолидиноны Эванса в синтезе.png|400px|center]]

== Developing ChemDraw ==
The widely used chemical structure drawing software package [[ChemDraw]] was initially conceived by Evans and was developed by a graduate student, Stewart Rubenstein, with input from Evans, his wife Sally, and the Evans research group for the preparation of the group's manuscripts.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Evans|first=David A.|date=October 13, 2014|title=History of the Harvard ChemDraw Project|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|language=en|volume=53|issue=42|pages=11140–11145|doi=10.1002/anie.201405820| pmid=25131311 |doi-access=free}}</ref> ChemDraw was premiered in July 1985 at the [[Gordon Research Conferences|Gordon Research Conference]] on Reactions & Processes in New Hampshire where Rubenstein and the Evanses demonstrated the new software during a break in the conference.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=BETHANY HALFORD |date=2014-08-18 |title=Reflections On ChemDraw |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1021/cen-09233-scitech1 |journal=Chemical & Engineering News Archive |volume=92 |issue=33 |pages=26–27 |doi=10.1021/cen-09233-scitech1 |issn=0009-2347|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
